question: What is the main goal of using inferential statistics in a research study?

options.A: Calculating the exact average age of every patient
options.B: Eliminating all possible errors from data collection
options.C: Generalizing sample findings to a larger population
options.D: Organizing raw data into simple frequency tables

explanation: Inferential statistics take data from a smaller group of participants and use it to draw conclusions about a much wider population. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why do researchers set up a null hypothesis before starting data analysis?

options.A: To prove that the new intervention is completely safe for pregnant women
options.B: To show that the sample size chosen is large enough for the study
options.C: To guarantee that the research findings will be statistically significant
options.D: To assume there is no real effect or difference until data proves otherwise

explanation: The null hypothesis acts as a baseline assumption that nothing changed or there is no effect, which statistical tests then check against. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which type of data works best for a parametric statistical test?

options.A: Nominal data like blood group types A, B, and O
options.B: Categorical data like male or female infant gender
options.C: Continuous numerical data like maternal height
options.D: Ranked data like mild, moderate, or severe pain

explanation: Parametric tests require continuous numerical measurements that follow a normal distribution. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h2)

question: What does homogeneity of variance mean when comparing groups?

options.A: Every single participant in the study has the exact same measurement
options.B: The sample size in the treatment group equals the control group
options.C: The data follows a strict bell-shaped curve without any outliers
options.D: The spread of data points is similar across all groups being compared

explanation: Homogeneity of variance simply means that the variability or spread of data is roughly equal across the different groups. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h2)

question: When would a researcher choose a non-parametric test instead of a parametric test?

options.A: When all assumptions of a normal bell-shaped distribution are fully met
options.B: When comparing the exact numerical means of continuous variables
options.C: When the data is heavily skewed or measured on an ordinal scale
options.D: When the researcher has a very large sample size exceeding one thousand

explanation: Non-parametric tests are designed for ranked, ordinal, or heavily skewed data that do not meet the rules of parametric tests. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why are non-parametric tests sometimes called distribution-free tests?

options.A: They do not require the data to follow a normal bell-shaped curve
options.B: They can be calculated without needing any numerical data at all
options.C: They eliminate the need for formulating a formal research hypothesis
options.D: They allow researchers to ignore missing participant records

explanation: These tests make no assumptions about the shape of the underlying population distribution. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which statistical test is best for comparing the average birth weight of babies born to teenage mothers versus older mothers?
explanation: An independent samples t-test compares the means of two separate, unrelated groups of people. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h4)

question: A researcher measures hemoglobin levels in pregnant women before and after a six-week malaria prevention program. Which test should she use to check for a change?
explanation: A paired samples t-test compares two sets of measurements taken from the exact same individuals at different times. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of using ANOVA instead of running multiple t-tests on three or more groups?

options.A: It eliminates the need for calculating standard deviations
options.B: It can analyze categorical data without numerical values
options.C: It requires a much smaller sample size to show significance
options.D: It prevents an increased risk of false positive errors

explanation: Running many t-tests at once raises the chance of a false positive result, which ANOVA helps prevent. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h5)

question: When is a one-way ANOVA appropriate for analyzing maternity research data?

options.A: Comparing mean blood loss across four different maternity clinics
options.B: Evaluating whether maternal age is correlated with gestational age
options.C: Testing the association between infant gender and delivery method
options.D: Comparing blood pressure readings before and after labor induction

explanation: One-way ANOVA is used when comparing the means of three or more separate groups. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h5)

question: What type of data is primarily analyzed using a Chi-Square test?

options.B: Exact time intervals in minutes or hours
options.C: Ranked pain scores on a continuous scale

explanation: The Chi-Square test evaluates categorical variables by looking at frequency counts in different categories. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h6)

question: What does a Chi-Square test compare to find its statistical value?

options.B: Median values of two completely independent groups
options.C: Sample mean values against population standard deviations
options.D: Variance within groups against variance between groups

explanation: The test measures how much the actual counts in a study differ from what would be expected by chance. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the FIRST thing a researcher should consider when choosing a statistical test?

options.A: The total budget available for conducting the research
options.B: The measurement scale and type of the data variables
options.C: The specific software program installed on the computer
options.D: The number of pages required for the final research report

explanation: The data type and scale determine whether parametric or non-parametric tests are appropriate. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h7)

question: A student wants to know if maternal smoking status (yes or no) is linked to low birth weight status (yes or no). Which test is NOT appropriate for this analysis?
explanation: An independent t-test is meant for continuous numerical data, whereas smoking status and birth weight are categorical variables that need a Chi-Square test. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T3#BMP225_U4_T3_h7)
